title: Unified Access, Change, and Procurement Manual
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Overview
--------
This manual consolidates core company-wide processes that span access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy touchpoints, and common internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for cross-functional operators (engineering, security, finance, and people-ops) to coordinate low-friction, auditable, and compliant workflows.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems.
- Covers lifecycle of requests: request -> approval -> fulfillment -> audit / revoke.
- Excludes specialized procedures documented on team-level pages (e.g., onprem packaging runbooks).

How to use this document
------------------------
- Follow the numbered processes for operational tasks.
- Use templates in Section "Library: Templates" for consistent submissions.
- Raise exceptions via the Risk & Exceptions flow (see "Related pages").

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
| Process | Primary owner | SLA (target) | Escalation owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access & permissions (standard) | IAM Platform | 48 business hours | Security Oncall |
| Emergency access (break-glass) | Security | immediate (0–2 hours) | SRE Lead |
| Change approvals (non-prod) | Engineering Change Board | 72 hours | Eng Platform Manager |
| Change approvals (prod) | Change Advisory Board (CAB) | 5 business days | CTO Office |
| Procurement (standard) | Procurement / Finance | 5 business days | Head of Finance |
| Vendor onboarding | Vendor Management | 7 business days | Legal Counsel |
| Expense reimbursements | Finance | 5 business days after submission | Finance Ops Lead |

1) Access & Permissions
-----------------------
Intro: Access requests should follow least-privilege principles. Roles are used where possible; adhoc grants must be timeboxed. All requests must include business justification and expiry.

Access classification
- Role-based: Preferred for services and groups (e.g., "redwood-data-analysts").
- Scoped token: Short-lived tokens for CI/CD jobs with automated rotation.
- Temporary elevation: Emergency / break-glass with audit.

Standard request flow (non-emergency)
1. User submits Access Request via the Access Portal (link: /confluence/eng-infra/access-portal). Include: resource, role, justification, org owner.
2. IAM Platform validates request (owner contact check).
3. Approver (owner_team lead) approves or rejects.
4. IAM Platform fulfills and assigns expiry (default 30 days for temporary requests).
5. Automated audit entry created in Audit Log stream.

Emergency (break-glass)
1. User requests emergency token via Security Slack channel + short form.
2. Security grants short-lived token (1 hour) and notifies CAB.
3. Post-incident: owner files retrospective and either approves extension or revokes.

RBAC examples and CLI snippets
- Grant role: redwoodctl iam grant --user priya.kapoor@redwood.ai --role redwood-data-analyst --resource dataset:traffic-logs
- Revoke role: redwoodctl iam revoke --user alice@redwood.ai --role redwood-maintainer

Access review cadence
- Quarterly review for high-privilege roles (SLA: 14 days to remediate mismatches).
- Annual org-wide certification for contractors.

2) Change Management
--------------------
Principles
- Changes are categorized by risk: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, EMERGENCY.
- Changes must include test plan, rollback plan, and observability signals.
- Production-facing changes require CAB approval; non-prod changes follow lightweight review.

Change request template (YAML example)
---
title: "upgrade-runtime-kernel-2026-02"
owner: "eng-platform"
category: "PROD"
risk: "MEDIUM"
planned_window: "2026-02-15T02:00:00Z/2026-02-15T04:00:00Z"
rollback_plan: |
  1) Disable new kernel via flag
  2) Redeploy previous image from tag v1.12.3
test_plan: |
  - end-to-end smoke: 100 requests/min for 15 minutes
observability: |
  - latency p95 < 200ms; error rate < 1%
---

Standard change workflow
1. Create change request in the Change Tracker with attached runbook and test artifacts.
2. Peer review and automated CI verification.
3. CAB reviews HIGH/PROD changes; non-PROD can be approved by owner.
4. Schedule during approved windows; notify affected teams.
5. Execute, monitor metrics and rollback if thresholds breached.
6. Post-change review within 5 business days.

Rollback thresholds (examples)
- Latency p95 increases by >2x for 5 minutes -> initiate rollback.
- Error rate >3% sustained for >2 min -> rollback.

3) Data Management
------------------
Classification levels
- PUBLIC: safe for external disclosure.
- INTERNAL: business data that is non-sensitive.
- CONFIDENTIAL: PII, model weights, customer data. Access requires justification, approved storage and encryption.

Storage & retention rules
- CONFIDENTIAL data must be stored in encrypted buckets with KMS-managed keys; retention default: 3 years unless contractually specified.
- Logs containing PII must be purged or redacted within 90 days.

Data handling checklist for new dataset
1. Classify dataset using Data Classification form.
2. Confirm legal/regulatory constraints with Legal.
3. Provision storage in approved project and enable server-side encryption.
4. Register dataset in the Data Catalog (link: /confluence/data-catalog).

Sample Data Classification table
| Field | Example | Classification | Storage requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| user_email | alice@example.com | CONFIDENTIAL | encrypted, access limited |
| telemetry_id | abc123 | INTERNAL | review quarterly |
| model_logits | float[] | CONFIDENTIAL | store in project with key rotation |

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Principles
- Central procurement ensures contract review, cost optimization, and vendor consolidation.
- Expense policy focuses on reasonableness and receipts for reimbursement.

Procurement flow (typical)
1. Team raises Purchase Request in Procurement Portal: justification, budget code, expected vendor.
2. Procurement verifies vendor, checks existing contracts, and obtains quotes.
3. Finance approves spend against budget.
4. Legal reviews contract if > $50k or if clauses flagged.
5. Procurement issues PO and tracks delivery.

Expense submission checklist
- Submit within 30 days of expense.
- Include itemized receipt and expense category.
- Use corporate card for business travel where available.

Per diem and travel guidance (high level)
- Domestic travel: meals up to $75/day.
- International: country-specific per diem on Travel Portal.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; business only with pre-approval.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Onboarding steps
1. Vendor Intake form: business case, regulatory needs, data access requirements.
2. Security assessment: fill vendor security questionnaire.
3. Contracting & SLAs: Legal drafts contract and defines SLAs and termination clauses.
4. Technical onboarding: assign minimal-access accounts and run PoC in sandbox.
5. Quarterly vendor review for strategic vendors.

Vendor risk categories & controls
- Low risk: SaaS with no customer data access. Controls: basic vendor profile and PO.
- Medium risk: vendors processing internal data. Controls: SOC2 report, contract clauses, least privilege.
- High risk: vendors accessing customer data or models. Controls: formal security assessment, encryption in transit+rest, dedicated VPC peering if required.

6) Travel Policy Highlights
--------------------------
- All work travel requires pre-approval via the Travel Portal.
- Travelers must submit expenses and trip summary within 10 business days of return.
- International travel with customer-sensitive data must consult Security for device posture.

7) Library: Templates
---------------------
Access Request template:
- title: Access request: <resource>
- requester: <name/email>
- resource: <resource identifier>
- role: <role requested>
- justification: <business reason>
- expiry: <date or duration>

Change Request minimal template (use in tracker):
- title, owner, window, risk, rollback_plan, test_plan, observability, impacted_services

Procurement request template:
- title, requester, budget_code, vendor, estimated_cost, justification, required_by, attachments

Vendor onboarding checklist (compact):
1) Intake form completed
2) Security questionnaire returned
3) Contract signed
4) Accounts provisioned (least privilege)
5) Kickoff and PoC schedule

Expense report minimal fields:
- claim_date, traveler, trip_purpose, receipts_attached (yes/no), total_amount, cost_center

Appendix: Exception & Audit Process
----------------------------------
- Exceptions are tracked in the Risk & Exceptions tracker; each exception must list compensating controls and an expiry date.
- Audits: IAM and Procurement logs are retained for 3 years and sampled quarterly.
